text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-A five-nation ceasefire monitoring committee will meet today to discuss a Lebanese complaint after Israeli shelling wounded six villagers in south Lebanon on Saturday.
The committee was established under an April 26 understanding which put an end to a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon.
-Hizbollah uncovers a 1992 "Israeli attempt to assassinate" its secretary general Sheikh Nasrallah.
-Government spending in 11 months reached 6,650 billion Lebanese pound. The budget deficit stood at 54.27 percent at the end of that period.
-Net public debt reached $10,067 million and foreign debt was $1,678 million at the end of November.
-Christian Maronite Patriarch Sfeir said there a big gap was dividing the poor and the rich in the country.
-Three Beirut gang members charged with making 15 billion Lebanese pounds by selling forged and genuine revenue stamps killed a finance ministry official party to the embezzlement.
-Speaker of Parliament Berri rejected President Hrawi's proposed constitutional amendments announced two weeks ago.
